newsitem.title: USA: NYSE Oct 28-Nov 1 program trading averages 11.6pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE Oct 28-Nov 1 program trading averages 11.6pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said Thursday that program trading for the week of October 28-November 1 was 11.6 percent of its average daily volume of 443.8 million shares, or 51.3 million shares a day.
For the prior week, program trading averaged 10.2 percent of average daily volume of 410.6 million shares, or 41.7 million shares a day.
Of the average 51.3 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for 31.5 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 19.8 million daily.
In all markets program trading averaged 73.5 million sharea a day during the week of October 28-November 1.

Of the five member firms reporting thte most program activity on the Big Board, First Options and Salomon Brothers executed all or more of their program activity for customers, as agents or facilitator. Lehman Brothers, First Boston and Morgan Stanley executed most of their program activity for their own accounts.
Between October 28 and November 1, 30.6 percent of program volume executed by NYSE member firms related to index arbitrage, while another 21.7 percent involved other derivative-related strategies.

Program volume executed on the exchange by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 57.2 percent during October 28-November 1. Program volume executed as principal, for their own acounts, amounted to 39.0 percent of program volume.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more, the exchange said.
